subject: AsterCore-13B intake: compatibility sprint & handoff
messages:
From: Ethan Simons <ethan.simons@asterlabs.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: eng-team@asterlabs.ai
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Intro: AsterCore-13B onboarding request

Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking a look — I work on infra at Aster Labs. We're preparing to put AsterCore-13B into customer-facing inference and would like Redwood to host/manage a model variant for us (primary ask: a 13B causal LM with a quantized "quant-lite" 4-bit variant plus a baseline fp16 variant). Key asks:

- Compatibility check with Redwood serving runtime (kv cache behavior, prefix caching).
- Any recommended quant profiles or known regressions for similar 13B architectures.
- SLO expectations for p95 latency at 1k tokens with dedicated dGPU pools.

I've attached the model_card (AsterCore-13B_model_card.pdf) and a small sample workload (sample_workload_snippets.json). We're also opening an SLA request; forwarding that as a doc (Aster_SLA_request.docx).

Can we get a 2-week compatibility sprint + a mutual action plan? Happy to join a short kickoff next week.

Best,
Ethan
Ethan Simons
Infra Lead, Aster Labs
ethan.simons@asterlabs.ai

Thanks Ethan — looping in infra (Dev) and applied ML (Vivek) to scope a compatibility sprint. Proposed plan:

1) Quick triage (48h): confirm model format + manifest, spot-check kv cache behavior with 512/2048 prefixes.
2) Sprint (10 business days): perf matrix (latency/cost), quant profile experiments, and a regression check suite against Redwood's safety/quality gate.
3) Deliverables: compatibility report, recommended quant profile, suggested rollout guardrails, and a canary roll runbook.

Dev/Vivek — please call out any blockers (HW, kernel gaps, tokenizer mismatch) and what artifacts you need from Aster. Ethan — we'll treat the attached docs as primary artifacts; Dev may ask for additional checkpoints.

I'll schedule a 30m kickoff Wednesday 2027-05-20 16:00 UTC unless you flag conflicts.

Thanks,

Spike notes and immediate asks:

Summary: From a serving infra perspective the artifacts look standard (HF-style model weights + config). Primary risks: attention kernel codepaths for custom rotary embeddings, and quantized KV cache stability with 4-bit flows — both are doable but require a focused test harness.

What I need from Aster to start the sprint:
- Model tarball (weights + tokenizer files) hosted temporarily (pre-signed URL) or a small sample checkpoint we can pull into staging.
- Specification of any custom ops or forked transformer blocks.
- Expected sequence length distribution (typical and tail). The sample_workload_snippets.json helps but we'll need a small corpus for perf runs (~1k queries).

Proposed infra checklist (deliverable within sprint):
- Pull & verify model artifacts (checksums).
- Run tokenization parity tests (Redwood tokenizer vs Aster tokenizer).
- Run KV cache stability run (24h continuous rolling load) on a staging node.
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latency for 128/512/1024 token contexts and capture memory spike events.

Attachments we'll drop into the sprint folder: redwood_intake_checklist.md, staging-run-command.sh, sample-perf-cmds.txt (I'll add these to the Confluence link).

Blockers/notes: if Aster requires private network peering for protected artifacts we need to loop in Security (this will add 2-4 business days). Also flagging that our 4-bit quant path is experimental for some custom rotary variants — will surface any differences in the final report.

Dev Patel
Infra Eng Lead, Redwood Inference

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, ethan.simons@asterlabs.ai
Date: 2027-05-20T15:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro: AsterCore-13B onboarding request

Initial compat readout (quick high-level):

- Tokenizer: whitespace+bytebpe variant — parity looks good after a small normalizer patch (1-line change to our tokenizer wrapper).
- Architecture: standard decoder-only transformer with rotary embeddings; no custom CUDA ops in the provided model_card. Good.
- Quantization: recommend two profiles to test in sprint: (A) norm-preserving 4-bit (our experimental path) and (B) 8-bit mixed precision as a baseline. Expect ~1.6x token throughput improvement on 4-bit but with a small risk of soft degeneration on long prefix chains; we'll surface regression tests.

Next steps I propose:
- Dev runs the KV stability script on a staging node (24h).
- I'll prep a prompt/regression set (50 prompts, eval harness) and run quality checks on fp16 vs quant-lite 4-bit.
- Lauren, please confirm if product needs Canary policy stricter than our default (we can add a stricter quality gate for the first 48h).

If no objections I'll run the first compatibility matrix starting Monday (2027-05-24) and we can review findings in a follow-up.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
